title: Edifício Copan
state: Original source reconstruction in progress; geographic and maximum-fidelity review pending

facts: Lists project year 1951 in São Paulo.
Distinguishes the residential block exterior from the altered executed program; the entire executed interior should not be attributed to the original design.
Restoration plans replace exterior ceramic mosaic with custom pieces matching original color, add drip edges to horizontal brises and beams, and repair concrete.
South facade cobogós are to be reproduced from molds of original pieces; metal window frames and commercial signs are included.
This describes restoration funding and planned work, not proof that restoration has finished.
Copan is listed at Avenida Ipiranga 200 and Rua Araújo 239 and 335.
Register protects exterior and common interior architecture; linked attachments may supply a parcel plan.

references.role: IBGE census field report, 2022-11-28; full article and selected photos inspected in browser
facts: Reports 115 m, 32 residential storeys, 1160 dwellings, 22 lifts, 72 shops and six blocks A–F.
Rooftop helipad was decommissioned because its dimensions were insufficient for landing.
The reported 2022 state had blue protective netting covering the building.

references.role: Bonfim and Oliveira, FAUUSP conservation study, 2020; PDF downloaded and pages 5 and 8 inspected
facts: Page 5 depicts separate curving residential plan, Block B external lift tower and round rear stairs; the principal brise facade is opposite the stairs.
Page 8 shows measured rear E/F facade: open helical stair flights with balustrades, repeated square cobogo openings, and shallow landings, not enclosed cylindrical stair towers.
The published section is a design archive drawing: the text documents major later alterations, so it cannot alone establish the executed podium.
White and gray porcelain mosaics and painted undersides require separate surface treatments.
The floor-plan graphic scale appears inconsistent with the mapped envelope and must be reconciled before using its absolute dimensions.

Page 12 photograph shows northwest end wall with two stacked columns of short horizontal slit openings, exposed curved podium decks/rails and the brise facade under protective netting. Its stripped cladding is a documented construction state, not the intended white-mosaic facade.

references.role: Original 2019 measured conservation thesis; public title/abstract found, PDF retrieval failed
facts: Potential primary source for brise section, material modules, as-built elevations and dimensions. Do not treat its uninspected measurements as verified.
Two photographs distinguish the densely glazed rear block from screened rear bays and open helical stairs.
Current portfolio labels work 2023–present; restoration completion is not established.

map.notes: Detailed S-shaped footprint includes rear stair projections. Height 118.44 and 37 levels differ from IBGE report; resolve the datums before use. Axis remains unsigned.

Find and inspect dimensioned plans/sections, separate basement/commercial/residential storey counts, and reconcile roof/parapet height.
Check current restoration state and explicitly choose a supported construction-state date.

visualReferences.observation: Ground-floor wayfinding plan photographed obliquely. Confirms A–F entrance labels and small square ceramic mosaic on the column. Unsuitable for dimension tracing.
Gallery has floor-to-ceiling retail glazing, dark metal security shutters and shallow fascia, continuous paved walkway and tiled piers.
Broad rear block has continuous glazing with thin transoms and narrower bay mullions; separate rounded white lift tower and open stair with radial treads.
Other rear blocks have projecting radial piers, inset perforated screen panels, upper windows, narrow horizontal slab bands, and open spiral stairs.

imagePolicy: Remote photos were viewed in browser only. Research PDF and rendered drawing pages remain ignored local references; no reference imagery is a model texture. The municipal promotional collage is not useful architectural evidence.

currentReview.scope: The original eleven-part GPU-instanced source assembly is preserved byte-for-byte and remains reconstructable from copan-model.mjs. Browser levels use four groups: shared ceramic mosaic, concrete and painted metal plus opaque glass. The principal S-curve, separate southern glass/screen blocks, lift capsule, three stair positions, 32-floor stack and roof platform remain. Near brise blades keep their outer 0.115 m lips with double-sided midplanes rather than hidden inner faces. Close-up retains all three blades per ordinary floor, original open transfer bands and 6 by 4 geometric perforations per panel; street retains blades with a coarser curve and 2 by 1 perforations every other floor; district has coarse eight-floor bands and 1 by 1 screens; skyline replaces dense fins with a closed midpoint facade proxy. Far podiums are closed shells. Near rear gallery glazing closes previously exposed gaps inside the mapped residential envelope; it is an approximate architectural closure, without a surveyed shop inventory. Close-up stairs retain twenty individual flat treads per reconstructed turn with continuous narrow handrail strips and alternate open pickets; the preserved source retains closed individual tread slabs, and precise stair risers, handedness and rail inventory remain unsurveyed. Street uses eight segments and district four; skyline uses small capped stair proxies whose external half-width remains within the one metre envelope allowance. All curves are deterministic adaptive polylines. Source white/gray ceramic finishes are the intended architecture, without temporary protection netting or a claim that restoration is complete. The modeled gallery follows the mapped residential envelope; the wider executed cinema/commercial site, neighboring bank and curved corner terraces require a separate site model and are excluded from this residential-block asset. Floor levels, transfer bands, screen dimensions, roof equipment and doors are reconstructions, not measured as-built details. Published height/level and plan-scale differences remain explicit. Flat grade is approximate. Physical phone/laptop and dense-city timings remain pending.
currentReview.placement: Fresh raw Q632566 way 8100248 independently matches the preserved 200-point ground ring within 0.002 m rounding. Anchor [-46.644483918,-23.546584452] and heading 0.390775195386 remain fixed; native +X points ENE at 67.61 degrees and +Z SSE at 157.61 degrees. The municipal restoration record independently calls the perforated cobogo facade the south facade. Raw coordinates place rear lift and stair projections on that side, opposite the principal northern brise curve (outline indices 0–64). The conservation plan and contractor photographs confirm the separate glazed rear block, screened rear blocks, one capsule lift tower and three open stair projections. Named southwest/northwest ends in the redrawn conservation plan are not used as compass controls: their reproduced page compass has not been reconciled with the raw site. Base Y0 is approximate local grade; actual street slope remains unsurveyed. Retain 115 m and 32 residential floors from the published IBGE record as the reconstruction basis; mapped 118.44 m and 37 total levels remain separately reported, without a surveyed datum reconciliation. No footprint replacement.
currentReview.primaryEvidence: Fresh architect foundation, conservation paper, contractor and municipal records read. Conservation pages 5, 8 and 12 and both contractor rear photographs actually inspected. IBGE facts remain from the retained prior primary record; fresh retrieval failed.
